notes: The arduino-leonardo catalogue entry lists no ports; port names '2' and 'GND' were used, following the Uno naming.

The circuit image is flipped relative to the catalogue's row convention. Rows f-j (bank 'b') are drawn at the top and rows a-e (bank 't') at the bottom. The button straddles the centre gap in columns 4 and 6.

The blue wire runs from pin 2 to column 6 in the top half (hole 6b.i). The black wire runs from GND to column 4 in the bottom half (hole 4t.c). The button therefore connects pin 2 to GND when pressed.
The mapping of the pushbutton's pins 1.l/1.r/2.l/2.r to breadboard holes is assumed from the image.
The USB cable to the computer is not shown in the images, so it is not included. The Leonardo is assumed to be powered over USB.
